provenance.author: Vincent Russo
provenance.method: slice-and-lift along a whole copy: the slice equations of every rank-3 decomposition of |CS>^2 admit only the identity assignment, and the assembled terms |CS> (x) u_i are not stabilizer states

compute.hardware: Apple silicon laptop, one core, under load from other jobs; about 45 s for the certificate

llm.role: wrote the block slice-and-lift and the certificate

notes: Upgraded from reproduced to verified (exact: true, we* + @mizopl, 2026-11-10, 2.6 s on one core, zero floating-point arithmetic) via verify_challenge/cert_cs_m3_m4_exact.py: applying (<0|_2 (I (x) H))^m to |CS>^m gives (2 sqrt(2))^(-m) |Psi_m> with |Psi_1> = 2|0> + (1+i)|1> in Z[i]^2 (checked symbolically against stabrank_verify.target_vector), so chi(|CS>^3) >= chi(|Psi_3>) = 4, certified both by D_2 slice-and-lift (483 rank-3 decompositions of |Psi_2>, 0 lifts) and by an unconditional 1,080-pivot Z[i] quotient sweep on D_3 (0 rank-3 decompositions, 4-state symmetric product positive control). Prior reproduced record (verify_challenge/cert_cs_m3_lift.py, ~45 s): puts 4 <= chi(|CS>^3) <= 6 (bounds/CS-m3-upper-6.json; note bounds/CS-m3-lower-5.json on main also certifies chi(|CS>^3) >= 5 at verified tier under budget_s: 3600). Slicing a rank-3 decomposition of |CS>^3 along its first copy (slice_lift.lifts_qubit_block) gives at each of the 4 slice values one of the 16 rank-3 decompositions of |CS>^2 (1 orbit under the order-1152 unitary symmetry group, 3 pivot orbits); each nonzero slice equation admits only the identity Pauli assignment with mu = alpha_a/alpha_00 = 1, 1, i, leaving |CS> (x) u_i which to_witness.term_from_vector rejects (numerical thresholds 1 - 1e-6 and 1e-7; controls on |T>^3 -> |T>^4, |H>^2 -> |H>^3, Bravyi-Kitaev T-type with |+>, and 15 rank-2 |CS> decompositions).
